We're starting to leave the territory where you'd test an LLM by e.g. "create an svg of pelican on a bicycle". As one idea to generalize it, I was interested what Opus 5 would do if I gave it the first paragraph of the Lord of the Rings, a 1M token budget (~$10) and asked for three js render of it. Opus went off for ~2 hours and wrote 5500 lines of code that (procedurally) rendered the story. It's kind of janky but fun. But it's a bit mindboggling that the LLM has to place and orchestrate various polygon assets in (x,y,z) coordinates and write code that animates it all, and that it even does anything at all.

I also like this kind of examples because no one in their right mind would ever spend the time to write something this custom but LLMs have all the stamina and patience in the world, so it's an example where we go from "no one would ever do this" to "sure, why not, it's ~free". There might be a lot more. But I'm excited about creating hyper custom worlds that you can imagine dropping players into, e.g. here to participate in the LoTR story as a spectator NPC, or one of the characters, or etc. Something like an ephemeral GTA of X on demand.

Last thought is that the domain of worlds/games exposes a weakness in LLMs: they can't easily audit their work because they aren't able to efficiently and natively perceive videos or play games within them. Here, Opus 5 had to very slowly and painstakingly take screenshots at different points, and it messed up a few times and created a bunch of jank. An example of raw capability (multimodal, gameplay) that I think is still quite lacking.

The @NYCMayor Mamdani pied a terre tax (the PAT tax) will likely reduce overall tax revenues for NY and that’s before considering the capital flight it will cause. 

When a NYC home is burdened with an additional annual tax, the home value will decline by the capitalized value of that new tax. 

While the PAT tax is set at 5%, it is 5% of the assessed value of the home, which is generally substantially less than its market value.  Assessed values are typically a fraction, let’s say 6%-15%, of the market value of a home and/or apartment so economically the PAT tax should be approximately 0.3%-0.75% of the market value of the home. 

Using a 4% cap rate, a 0.3%-0.75% PAT tax should reduce market values and annual real estate tax collections by 7.5%-18.75% assuming people believe the tax will be payable annually over the long term. 

The impact on current real estate values is not just on owners whose primary residence is elsewhere. As such, the value of all NYC residential real estate is going to decline. This will lead to substantially reduced assessed values and lower overall real estate tax collections. 

And all of the above is before considering capital flight as more wealthy NYers leave the city and the desirability of NYC residential real estate declines. 

Tell me why I am wrong.

The reason I don’t tell anyone to go all in bitcoin or any single asset and to own other assets (at least 3 )is not from a lack of belief or understanding 

It’s because precisely for the fact as we have seen that each asset - depending on its qualities has different downsides and upsides  

Ie you may own property in a country that ends up in a war or earthquake even if fundamentals are great - you could own something and it gets confiscated by the government or taxed and regulated to death or lose from loss of trust in the currency

Similarly the number 1 reason for not being all in btc is the agency component - you could be right and still lose due to losing wallet/keys etc

Every asset has its upside and downside - In Bitcoin the downside is in wallet control which is why the thesis is the improvement in infrastructure to better support and mitigate it over time aswell 

As we saw even the biggest technical  advocates have blind spots 

You must acknowledge to yourself that no matter how much you think you know there is always a blind spot 

We can’t mitigate all things but consciously going through different scenarios upfront will help 

I’m concerned with the trend of these all in one stock etc traders aswell as they preach “it’s only if you don’t know what you are doing” 

The problem is because you “know” what you are doing that you lose - the inability to see how you could get slaughtered

My general view on hardware wallets is the same as exchanges 

Generally using the largest and well known is better than obscure 

1)if there is a hack on a smaller brand you are on your own with very little resources - if you use a big brand and there is a wide hack there is immense resources to both increase awareness, recover and find culprits aswell as incentive to refund losses 

2)if a large provider suffers a massive hack the whole space is screwed for a while anyway being on an obscure wallet wasn’t going to save you from downside in price 

3) psychologically it’s easier to deal with loss when everyone is on same boat 

4)if an industry wide drop happens like ftx style prices get so low that even if you lost from the major hack just investing a fraction from elsewhere can recreate your position if it’s a temporary issue 

There are so many considerations outside of just security in a technical sense 

These are just some things to consider
